blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Abbotsford total for houses that month.

blocks.text: Listings of houses in Abbotsford West fell from 141 in June to 115 in October (−18.4%), and 76 sold across the 5 months. In October the community held 28.0% of Abbotsford’s 410 houses listed.

blocks.text: Abbotsford West Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: The west side's working edges in City material are Mt. Lehman Road at Highway 1 Exit 83, Clearbrook Road at Exit 87, Maclure Road, Townline Road and Blueridge Drive, with the Highstreet Transit Exchange site on Highstreet Access Road between Mt. Lehman Road and Cardinal Avenue marking the northwest corner.

blocks.text: Abbotsford West Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Westerleigh is the west side's named master-planned community, and developer Polygon Homes describes it as an established community beside the Discovery Trail, the all-season corridor connecting the east and west ends of the city, with the Club West clubhouse at its centre.

Blue Jay Elementary at 30995 Southern Drive opened in September 1988, and the school's own history page records that the surrounding streets are named after birds — Robin, Sandpiper, Sparrow, Curlew, Osprey, Cardinal, Swallow, Heron and Mallard.

blocks.text: Abbotsford West Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A house with a suite needs extra parking, and the Zoning Bylaw requires a minimum of two parking spaces for a single family house plus one additional space if a secondary suite is constructed.

blocks.text: Abbotsford West Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Non-catchment school requests are restricted at W.J. Mouat Secondary and all its feeder schools, and SD34 states it has restricted those requests to reduce enrolment over time — a west-side address outside the Mouat catchment is not a reliable route into that school.
Westerleigh houses sit beside the Discovery Trail, which Polygon Homes describes as an all-season corridor connecting the east and west ends of the city.

blocks.text: Abbotsford West Houses: development and new projects

items.t: The Highstreet Transit Exchange is under construction on Highstreet Access Road, and the City states construction is underway for an exchange with six bus bays, accessible wide sidewalks, shelters and benches, improved street lighting, crosswalk and wayfinding signage, bicycle amenities, street trees and landscaping. Status read 2026-11-03: under construction.

blocks.text: Abbotsford West Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: Houses inside the Urban Storm Drainage Area also pay a storm drainage service fee, set for 2026 at 0.11615 per $1,000 for Class 1 residential properties with improvements over $5,000.

blocks.text: Abbotsford West Houses: getting around

items.t: Highway 1 is the west side's through route, and the City's transit exchange page places the Highstreet site between Mt. Lehman Road (Exit 83) and Cardinal Avenue, serving routes #1, #2 and #66 Fraser Valley Express.

Route 21 links the west side to Aldergrove and to central Abbotsford, running between Aldergrove and Bourquin Exchange via Highstreet, with stops at Fraser Highway at Lefeuvre Road and at South Fraser Way at Clearbrook Road.
The Discovery Trail gives the Westerleigh area an off-road walking and cycling link, described by Polygon Homes as an all-season corridor connecting the east and west ends of the city.

blocks.text: Abbotsford West Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the lot's zone and floodplain status for the specific parcel rather than the street, because the bylaw's floodproofing areas are mapped on Schedule "E" and apply by mapped area, not by neighbourhood name.

blocks.text: Abbotsford West home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

118 houses sold in Abbotsford West with a median price of $1,023,564 (the middle half sold between $927,075 and $1,137,500), taking a median of 19 days to sell at 95.9% of the last list price; 3% sold above list. They had a median $403 per square foot, a median year built of 1986 and a median lot of 6,960 square feet.

blocks.text: Jared's take on Abbotsford West
Older houses west of Clearbrook Road and strata homes clustered around South Fraser Way and Sevenoaks give Abbotsford West, the Clearbrook side, its mix. It’s the city’s biggest attached market.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Abbotsford West?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 115 houses listed in Abbotsford West. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Abbotsford West a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses in Abbotsford West had a sales ratio of 18%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many houses sold in Abbotsford West from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 76 houses sold in Abbotsford West over those 5 months, out of 287 in all of Abbotsford.

faq.q: Does this page include townhomes or duplexes in Abbotsford West?
faq.a: No. The figures are for detached houses only. Condos and townhomes are counted on their own page.

faq.q: What did houses in Abbotsford West sell for?
faq.a: 118 houses sold in Abbotsford West between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,023,564.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Abbotsford West?
faq.a: The median was 19 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 95.9% of the last list price (3% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
